q: An organization needs a dedicated security control to inspect incoming HTTP requests and protect public-facing web servers from application-layer attacks like SQL injection. Which technology best meets this requirement?
opts: Stateful perimeter packet filtering firewall
Virtual private network encryption gateway
Dedicated web application firewall appliance
Forward proxy content filtering cache server
exp: A Web Application Firewall (WAF) operates at Layer 7 to inspect incoming HTTP/HTTPS traffic, blocking web attacks like SQLi and XSS before they reach the server.

wrongFeedback.0: Stateful packet filtering firewalls operate primarily at Layers 3 and 4 (IP addresses and ports), lacking deep inspection capabilities for HTTP application-layer payloads.
wrongFeedback.1: A VPN gateway encrypts network communications between endpoints, providing secure remote access rather than filtering malicious web payloads.
wrongFeedback.3: A forward proxy regulates outbound employee web browsing requests, whereas protecting public-facing web servers requires inspecting inbound traffic.

q: A critical zero-day vulnerability is discovered in an enterprise web app's login form. Testing a permanent code patch will take two weeks. Which action provides the fastest compensating control to block exploitation immediately?
opts: Implementing a custom pattern-matching rule on the reverse proxy WAF
Migrating the backend database cluster into an isolated internal subnet
Enforcing full disk encryption across all active production web instances
Revoking active administrative session tokens from edge network routers
exp: A WAF allows administrators to deploy "virtual patches" by creating custom Layer 7 signature or regex rules that filter out attack patterns before requests reach the vulnerable application code.

wrongFeedback.1: Isolating the database is good segmentation practice, but it does not prevent an attacker from exploiting the web app's login logic from the outside.
wrongFeedback.2: Full-disk encryption protects data at rest against physical drive theft; it provides zero protection against live application-layer exploits.
wrongFeedback.3: Revoking router administration tokens secures network infrastructure management, but has no effect on incoming public web requests targeting the web application.

q: An enterprise deploys an inline WAF to protect a customer portal, but security logs reveal that SQL injection attacks sent over HTTPS pass through undetected. What configuration is missing on the WAF?
opts: Binding user directory memberships to stateful firewall routing tables
Restricting incoming web traffic to verified internal RFC 1918 subnets
Enabling continuous transaction rollback routines on backend databases
Terminating TLS sessions using the web server's private certificate
exp: Because HTTPS encrypts payload contents end-to-end, an inline WAF cannot inspect HTTP headers or query strings without terminating TLS, which requires installing the web server's private certificate.

wrongFeedback.0: Mapping user identities to firewall rules (User-ID) authenticates internal users, but does not enable the inspection of encrypted web traffic payloads.
wrongFeedback.1: Restricting traffic to RFC 1918 (private) subnets would block legitimate public internet customers from reaching the public portal.
wrongFeedback.2: Database rollbacks preserve transaction integrity during execution errors, but do not inspect or block incoming malicious web traffic.

q: An attacker submits an SQL injection payload using double URL encoding (%2527). The WAF fails to detect the attack and passes it to the database, where it successfully executes. Why did the WAF fail to block this request?
opts: The database engine automatically bypassed application-level validation
The WAF evaluated raw input strings without recursively decoding the data
The reverse proxy dropped HTTP response headers during transport routing
The application server processed the request over an unencrypted channel
exp: If a WAF decodes input only once, %2527 resolves to %27, which does not match a plain quote (') signature. If the backend application performs a second decode pass, the payload executes unless the WAF applies recursive normalization.

wrongFeedback.0: Databases execute whatever queries are passed to them; they do not selectively bypass application filters on their own initiative.
wrongFeedback.2: Dropping HTTP response headers affects data sent back to the client, not how incoming request payloads are inspected.
wrongFeedback.3: Running over an unencrypted channel (HTTP) makes payload inspection easier for a WAF, not harder; the failure here stems from encoding evasion, not encryption.

q: An organization needs to prevent cross-site request forgery and cookie tampering on its customer portal. Why does the security architect require a dedicated WAF rather than relying on the perimeter NGFW?
opts: A WAF inspects network routing protocols to block spoofed IP addresses
A WAF provides automated endpoint isolation for infected client laptops
A WAF specializes in inspecting HTTP session state, cookies, and headers
A WAF enforces static access control policies based on user job roles
exp: While NGFWs possess application awareness, dedicated WAFs specialize in deep HTTP/HTTPS analysis, including parsing session cookies, validating anti-CSRF tokens, and inspecting web application parameters.

wrongFeedback.0: Inspecting Layer 3 routing protocols (like BGP or OSPF) is a router or network firewall capability, not a web application security function.
wrongFeedback.1: Isolating infected client devices is a function of Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), not a web gateway control.
wrongFeedback.3: Enforcing role-based access control (RBAC) is an identity and directory management function, not the operational distinction between NGFWs and WAFs.
